topic: What limitations might arise from the close frequency spacing in practical satellite applications despite high inter-channel isolation?
consensus_response: Close frequency spacing leads to spatial interference effects due to the receive array's inability to resolve each transmit antenna, causing the MIMO channel to converge to a keyhole channel with h ≈ a. This results in severe degradation of the achievable Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio (SINR), which depends on the User Terminal (UT) position. The reduced SINR translates to reduced capacity and increased complexity for interference mitigation techniques, increasing the 'cost' of system performance.
reference_context: Close frequency spacing leads to severe spatial interference due to reduced SINR, causing the MIMO channel to converge to a keyhole channel with h ≈ a. This results in accumulation of created interference, degrading achievable SINR and capacity.
